findings.title: Dirty Frag: Universal Linux LPE (oss-security, original disclosure)
findings.summary_md: Hyunwoo Kim posted the Dirty Frag report to oss-security on May 7, 2026 at 18:56 UTC, publishing at the linux-distros maintainers' request after the disclosure embargo was broken by a third party. The post states no patches or CVEs existed at publication, chains the xfrm-ESP and RxRPC page-cache write flaws, links the upstream ESP fix commit f4c50a4034e6, and gives a modprobe blacklist with rmmod for esp4, esp6 and rxrpc as the only mitigation. Full exploit source is embedded in the message.

findings.title: V4bel/dirtyfrag public exploit repository
findings.summary_md: The dirtyfrag.io documentation referenced from the disclosure resolves to this repository, which holds the public exploit exp.c with a one-line build (gcc -O0 -Wall -o exp exp.c -lutil), an affected-version matrix, and mitigation and cleanup notes. GitHub records repository creation at 2026-05-07T18:18:28Z, roughly 38 minutes before the oss-security post. The README documents post-exploitation cleanup with echo 3 > /proc/sys/vm/drop_caches or a reboot because the exploit contaminates the page cache.

findings.title: xfrm: esp: avoid in-place decrypt on shared skb frags (netdev/net commit f4c50a4034e6)
findings.summary_md: Kuan-Ting Chen's fix, dated May 4, 2026 in the netdev net tree, documents the ESP-half root cause: MSG_SPLICE_PAGES can attach pipe pages directly to an skb, the IPv4/IPv6 datagram append paths did not set SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG, and ESP input then took the no-COW fast path and decrypted in place over pages the skb did not own. The patch marks spliced frags with SKBFL_SHARED_FRAG and forces ESP input back to skb_cow_data() when the flag is present. No distribution kernel shipped this change at the time of the Dirty Frag disclosure.

findings.title: esp4: Avoid skb_cow_data whenever possible (introducing commit cac2661c53f3)
findings.summary_md: Steffen Klassert's January 17, 2017 change made esp4 skip skb_cow_data on the fast path, and the Dirty Frag disclosure scopes the affected window for the xfrm-ESP page-cache write from this commit to the May 2026 fix, roughly nine years of exposure across mainline kernels. This is the origin of the ESP half of the chain.

findings.title: splice, net: Use sendmsg(MSG_SPLICE_PAGES) rather than ->sendpage() (commit 2dc334f1a63a)
findings.summary_md: David Howells' June 2023 conversion of the generic splice send paths to sendmsg with MSG_SPLICE_PAGES is the change the disclosure document scopes as the start of the affected window for the RxRPC page-cache write. It moved pipe-backed page splicing into the networking send paths the RxRPC half of the chain relies on.
